title: Isolation and Characterization Of Chimeric Human Fc-expressing Proteins Using Protein A Membrane Adsorbers And A Streamlined Workflow
protocol: Verify that the Fc-expressing protein has acceptable affinity for protein A.
Test for the presence of the protein in the stock solution.
Use flow cytometry, Western blotting, or ELISA to detect protein function and/or presence of Fc.
Quantify the protein in the cell culture supernatant.
Prepare the protein A membrane adsorber according to manufacturer instructions.
Ensure no air enters the membrane adsorber during preparation.
Perfuse DPBS through the membrane adsorber to remove storage solution and equilibrate it.
Filter the cell culture supernatant immediately before perfusion using a 0.22 µm sterile filtration unit.
Aspirate cell culture supernatant into a Luer Lock syringe and discharge any air bubbles.
Connect the syringe to the inlet of the membrane adsorber.
Attach flexible tubing to the membrane adsorber outlet.
Set the syringe pump to the desired volumetric flow rate without exceeding the manufacturer's recommended flow rate.
Perfuse the cell culture supernatant through the membrane adsorber, collecting flow through in a container.
Reload the syringe with supernatants as needed.
Wash the membrane adsorber with 10 ml DPBS to remove any nonbound protein.
Elute protein from the membrane adsorber at the desired flow rate using 10-15 ml of elution buffer.
Catch the eluate in a tube containing neutralizing buffer at 10% of the elution volume.
Elute protein in 1 ml increments into tubes containing 100 µl neutralization buffer using a total volume of 10-15 ml elution buffer.
Test each fraction for the presence of protein using the preferred characterization method.
Regenerate the membrane adsorber according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Perfuse 10 ml of 0.22 μm-filtered DPBS or buffer of choice through the membrane adsorber.
Perfuse 10 ml of 0.22 μm-filtered 50 mM NaOH in 1 N NaCl through the membrane adsorber.
Perfuse 10 ml of 0.22 μm-filtered DPBS through the membrane adsorber.
Fill the membrane adsorber with 20% ethanol in DPBS for long-term storage at 4°C.
Concentrate all eluate or elution fractions containing protein using a centrifugal filter unit.
Dialyze the retentate in a small volume dialysis unit against the buffer of choice following manufacturer's instructions.
Resolve purified protein and Fc standards on a mini gel by SDS-PAGE under reducing or nonreducing conditions as desired.
Determine the Fc standards range over which band signal varies linearly with respect to quantity of loaded.
Use the same gel, running conditions, transfer conditions, and reagents for quantifying and characterizing purified protein.
Load multiple sample amounts of purified protein, including samples diluted with DPBS.
Transfer proteins from the gel to a PVDF membrane in a discontinuous buffer system using a semidry blotter.
Follow the blotter manufacturer's instructions during transfer.
Transfer time is typically 5-10 min.
Coomassie stain the gel after transfer to verify transfer efficiency if desired.
Perform immunoblotting with anti-Fc or anti-IgG conjugated to alkaline phosphatase (AP) or horse radish peroxidase (HRP).
Use a vacuum-assisted protein detection system for immunoblotting.
Immunoblotting time is typically less than 1 hr.
Develop an immunoblot using the substrate and method of choice.
Quantify purified protein by image analysis.
Perform a linear regression on the band signals from Fc standards.
If R2>0.90, use the equation for the line to calculate protein quantity from its band signal(s).
Account for sample dilution if necessary.
Adjust the value for molecular weight differences between the protein and Fc.
If R2<0.90, repeat step 6 in its entirety.
Validate protein using functional assays or methods to detect Fc via flow cytometry, Western blotting, ELISA, etc.
Dilute protein to desired concentration.
Add any desired preservatives or stabilizers to the purified protein solution.
Aliquot the solution for long-term storage.
Store aliquots frozen or otherwise as appropriate.
